Key dates

  • In-person early voting: October 5, 2026 to November 2, 2026. Vote early in person at your county clerk or election commission office.
  • Voter registration deadline: October 16, 2026. Last day to register online, by mail, at a state agency, or through a deputy registrar or personal agent. Today, October 23, is the last day to register in person at your county election office, until 6 p.m. local time.
  • Last day to request an early (mail) ballot: October 23, 2026. Your county election office must receive your early ballot application by 6 p.m. local time today. Completed ballots are due back to the county election office by the time polls close on Election Day.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls are open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Central Time (7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Mountain Time). You need a photo ID to vote.

Official election information: Nebraska Secretary of State – Elections

Who's running

Only the U.S. Senate and governor races are loaded so far. Other statewide offices, ballot measures, U.S. House and local races aren't loaded yet. Check your sample ballot for the full list.

Federal

United States Senator

This seat has a six-year term. Incumbent Pete Ricketts, appointed in 2023 and elected in the 2024 special election, is running for a full term.

Mike Marvin is on the certified list but has been reported as no longer running. Check your sample ballot.

  • Chuck Conboy America First · Challenger
  • Mike Marvin Legal Marijuana NOW · Challenger
  • Dan Osborn By Petition · Challenger
  • Robin Richards Nebraska Working People · Challenger
  • Pete Ricketts Republican · Incumbent
State

Governor and Lt. Governor

This office has a four-year term, and each governor candidate runs on a joint ticket with a lieutenant governor. Incumbent Jim Pillen is running for re-election. The running mates are Joe Kelly (Pillen, Republican), Ben Steffen (Walz, Democratic), Keenya Barnes (Beard, Legal Marijuana NOW) and Michael Picard (Lindstrom, America First).

  • Rick Beard Legal Marijuana NOW · Challenger
  • Brett Lindstrom America First · Challenger
  • Jim Pillen Republican · Incumbent
  • Lynne Walz Democratic · Challenger
